standard.title: Present descriptions and explanations
standard.description: present descriptions and explanations, using ideas from sources and relevant subject-specific terms
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S07): Students presented using ideas from sources and subject-specific terms from history, geography and civics.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present descriptions and explanations using ideas from sources and subject-specific terms from Year 4 HASS disciplines.

nodes.label: Year 4 subject-specific vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use accurate Year 4 subject-specific terms from history, geography and civics in speech, writing and illustration.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two terms from each of two HASS disciplines accurately in a description or explanation.
nodes.typical_width: Use historical terms (exploration, navigation, trade, penal, transportation, contact, colonisation); geographical terms (continents, countries, natural resources, vegetation, environments, ecosystems, sustainability, consumption, waste, management); civic terms (local government, decision-making, services, roles, responsibilities, rules, laws, belonging).
wider: Use subject-specific vocabulary to write a multi-disciplinary explanation of a single event (e.g. colonisation) from historical, geographical and civic perspectives
Create a subject-specific vocabulary resource that includes definitions, examples and images for Year 4 HASS
nodes.hinge_reason: Year 4 introduces significantly more complex and specific vocabulary across all three disciplines — without this vocabulary, students cannot communicate at the level the descriptor demands.

response_modes.reason: Year 4 vocabulary includes many abstract and discipline-specific terms requiring sustained practice — use word walls, explicit instruction and vocabulary-embedded inquiry tasks.

success_criteria: Uses at least two subject-specific terms from at least two disciplines accurately
Terms are used in disciplinary context (not just listed)

nodes.label: Describing relative location and direction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the relative location of different features in a place by distance and compass direction.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the location of at least two places or features using distance and at least one compass direction.
nodes.typical_width: Describe relative location using distance and compass direction (e.g. the distance from home to local waste management site; the route of a navigator); incorporate spatial descriptions into presentations about historical events and geographical features.
wider: Describe a complete route from one place to another using compass directions and distance estimates
Incorporate a map with compass directions into a presentation and explain location using both the map and verbal description

response_modes.reason: Relative location description with compass direction integrates spatial literacy with HASS communication — the presentation is the integration task.

success_criteria: Describes the location of at least two features using distance and compass direction
At least one compass direction is used correctly
